Chief Complaint
Establish care

History of Present Illness
The patient is a [AGE] female with a history of fibromyalgia, depression, hypothyroidism, and a past stroke, presenting for an established care visit. Fibromyalgia and Torn Rotator Cuff The patient reports worsening fibromyalgia symptoms, particularly exacerbated by the current weather. She states that neither her pain patch nor Oxycodone are providing adequate relief. She is interested in trying new treatments. The patient is aware of the importance of aerobic exercise but is limited due to a torn rotator cuff. She engages in stretching and as much exercise as she can tolerate. She is scheduled to start therapy at [ORGANIZATION] soon, as referred by [PERSON]. Depression The patient has been on sertraline for depression for 30 years, which she reports is working well. She is willing to try duloxetine for her fibromyalgia. Hypothyroidism The patient continues to manage her hypothyroidism with medication. She did not report any new issues related to this condition during the visit. Stroke The patient had a stroke approximately [AGE], which resulted in left-sided paralysis for three to four days. She still experiences some left-sided weakness. She was not on any medication for stroke prevention, including aspirin. Cholesterol The patient has a history of high cholesterol, with markedly elevated total cholesterol and LDL on prior testing. She had been on statins but was taken off them by a previous doctor. Sleep Apnea The patient has sleep apnea and uses a CPAP machine. She reports some memory issues. The patient has a family history of Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, and dementia, which she is concerned about. Toenail Issues The patient has been using antifungal treatment for her toenails, which are raising up. She finds it difficult to trim her nails due to her hip issues.

Physical Exam
Vitals & Measurements HR: 59 BP: 118/74 SpO2: 96% HT: 163.9 cm WT: 69.30 kg BMI: 25.8 No acute distress. Normocephalic. Conjunctiva not injected. Cooperative affect. She does have some mild nail thickening (L foot #1, 3,4) and mild pincer changes on L #1.

Assessment/Plan
Patient is a [AGE] female with a history of fibromyalgia, hypothyroidism, and a past CVA, presenting today for fibromyalgia management and routine care. Sounds like this last happened in [YEAR] - several days of symptoms, including speech and mobility. Not currently on aspirin. I would recommend she take 1 of those. Baby aspirin daily. Hyperlipidemia. Her last lipids showed LDL greater than 200–repeat in consider lipid-lowering agents. GERD–doing okay off medications as well. Hypothyroidism. Last thyroid level showed mild suppression of her TSH–will repeat. Opioid use. No change in her fentanyl and oxycodone. Fibromyalgia. She reports increasing pain from this. Trial of duloxetine 20 mg twice daily consider tapering up if works okay. Depression–doing well on her EsCitalopram–we will cut that down to 100 mg daily and consider tapering further if we taper off duloxetine. Asthma–very infrequent use of her inhaler even during this current allergy season–follow-up. Sleep apnea–continues on CPAP and tolerating okay. Memory problems. I did point out that her opioids may have an effect here. She is getting neurology evaluation in the future. Health maintenance–PCV immunization today. I spent over 30 minutes in the face-to-face, and documentation of this visit today.
